Desirous of illustrating my using that example -- well, when the investigators arrived there, that is, the AID brought witnesses for them, and told them about the events in Sovici and Doljani on the 17th of April, because naturally they wouldn't be mentioning their own crimes. And there, that is how one begins to manipulate things. But not only in that particular case. To my mind, the major manipulation was done with the 16th of April because before the 16th of April, long before it, before even January, 1993, not to speak about the events in 1992, the BH Army launched attacks over a very large territory, both in central Bosnia and in Konjic, in Konjic and Jablanica, cleansed the Neretvica valley right down to Mostar long before the 16th of April, when Safet Cibo came and he was appointed directly by Alija Izetbegovic himself as the wartime president in disregard of all legal or any other powers, and series of crimes were committed which I mentioned in my opening brief and about which we heard from various witnesses, I will not waste my time on this. And then they tried to cover it up with a so-called tu quoque defence and we know what tu quoque Defence is as if a fool said well, He killed my father, so I may kill his father. That's what it is. But only a fool would defend himself or herself like this. But here insistence is made on this principle in order to conceal what truly happened, because there are always causal relationship, nothing has fallen out of the blue sky, and nothing happened by accident. And that is how an attempt was made to concept, to cover up the events that I mentioned before, the events in Mostar. We heard witnesses who were in camps on the eastern side, no indictment, there is no indictment for these camps, nor will there ever be one. The persecution of Croats on the east bank, 10.000 of them if it was a persecution or was it a war, and there is no indictment, nor there will ever be one. And that was all about the objectivity that I wanted to say, because had this been objective then, this case would have looked completely different -- not only that it would have looked different, but my client would have never appeared here. Your Honours, it is your duty to decide, having heard the case, whether Mladen Naletilic was a person who had committed a specific crime on the basis of unambiguous evidence, that is only by individualising the responsibility and only through the individualisation of responsibility can we arrive at the truth but this individualisation of responsibility needs to be established by you on the basis of evidence. I wish to point out that the Prosecution does not justify, does not dispute, that there were crimes committed during the conflict between the BH Army and the HVO. The Defence does not think that a crime is justifiable. The crime -- the Defence deems that those who committed the crime need to be held responsible for those crimes on both sides. And those victims cry out for justice. A victim will not be happy, will not rest satisfied, if an innocent person is accused. What may not be forgotten is that today, that is nine or ten years after the conflict, one needs to make an effort and imagine a situation which reign at the time covered by the indictment. A war -- war is a special situation in which unfortunately the sense of values change and people lose ability to take rationale decisions. War entails victims. One loses one's next of kin, one's life is constantly at stake, there is no safe place where one can look and analyse the situation objectively. As a rule, one remembers the names of the first victims of war. After that, one moves on to numbers and says, "Well, this unit lost so many and the other one so many." Now, can you please try to imagine Mostar, not on the 9th of April, because that is not when the war started, that is also one of the insinuations. The war started on the 30th of June, and on both occasions the attack was launched by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you imagine a city where shelling and gun fire are daily occurrences? Can you imagine a situation when somebody is killed by a sniper bullet or by a shell day in and day out? And I mean women and children and soldiers, in the city of Mostar, and I mean equally on its east and on its west bank. Can you -- can you imagine such a -- can you conjure up the image of this Mostar and think about it? And here, insistence is made on the finest possible processes of a state with a rule of law, the oldest democracies and states which have been in existence for, I don't know how many centuries, even when such a thing happens in their countries, many more are suspended and a state of war is proclaimed, and here we do not have a state. This state doesn't exist. So which police, what courts, who -- what is going on there? Who is the one who can bring some order? The greatness of the HZ HB and HR HB was in its attempt to try to make some order in a state which is not. They adopted laws because there were none. All the laws that there were available came from the socialist period, the new assembly had not and had time to adopt them. The moment when the state's external borders were recognised, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it disintegrated. There were no laws, there was no police in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not exist. Fortunately, the HZ HB established some kind of defence shield. It saved not itself but the whole population against the aggression, and managed to provide some kind of order so that it could function normally. Do we have this picture before our eyes? Here, the OTP, referring to those situations, speaks as if it was some England -- as if it was London, 1945, and then such a nation democracies organising life in London. And then they look at -- they scrutinise every tiny detail forgetting that people were seeking -- were running for their life on all sides. What happened in Mostar, briefly and clearly: Two armies were fighting over positions. And what was the role of Mladen Naletilic, if any, there? According to the Prosecutor, crucial one. What evidence? The war lord in Herzegovina? On the basis of what evidence? According to the OTP, the world is obviously black and white, except that in the conflict in 1993, the Muslims were white and the Croats black. The notorious good and bad guys but in the real world and we all know it very well, there is no black and white, everything is grey, more or less, which means that both sides to the -- both parties to the conflict were living on the brink of death all the time. And both parties made moves which -- in which they take no pride now, ten years later. If the Defence has showed what happened to the Croats during the conflict with the Muslims, it didn't do it in order to justify anyone, but to show that war is a terrible thing for everyone, the terrible things that happened to everybody during the war and that it is not objective what the OTP tries to show, that only one side was a victimised. Of course, not trying to belittle in any way, not for a single moment, the victims of the war and real victims on the side of the Bosnian Herzegovinian Muslims, but that is one side. The other side of it is whether Mr. Mladen Naletilic was indeed what the OTP claims he was or is it -- was he simply selected by the AID to be offered to the OTP as the crucial figure? When one carefully analyses the evidence that the OTP backs its argument -- uses to back its argument, it is not possible, one cannot really conclude judiciously that Mladen Naletilic is responsible for the crimes he is being charged with. So now I will quote to you an example, a document DD 1206.1. I think -- yes, that's right. It is P, actually it is document P206.1, which the OTP produced and they rather timidly produced it toward the end of the case. It clearly says that on the 23rd of December, 1992, Mario Hrkac, Cikota, was the commander of the Convicts Battalion. It is a document from the archive, and then again, the Prosecutor doesn't stop claiming the opposite in spite of this. Well, you can't do it. The OTP can't say: "This is a good document if it fits into his picture and if it doesn't, say not. How can we have from the one and the same archive when we have this clearly document -- inculpatory document and it should have been disclosed to us earlier, but of course it wasn't. But this document doesn't say only this thing, it also says other things. It says that the Convicts Battalion has 54 members, all the Defence has been claiming and showing through its case. It says other professional units, which again, the Defence clearly showed in this courtroom that there were three, four professional units, first Bruno Busic, Ludvig Pavlovic, Baja Kraljevic, and the Convicts Battalion in 1992, and in 1993, the Convicts Battalion leaves as an ATG for their operative zone, to the brigade such as the whole defence system of the HZ HB, which in contrast with the BH Army, who were organised in corps, the former was organised in operative zone, that is home guard, the defence of one's village, town, hearth, field on the home guard principle, and every such brigade had one ATG. And those three professional -- professional units. We've heard a great deal about subordination, who comes, who goes, the role of this and the role of that, who goes to the ground, who goes to the front line, who is attached to whom, what are the chains of command, and so on and so forth. But no, even after that, that does not matter, but I hope that it will matter to the Chamber. Furthermore, what is the document that confirms unambiguously that Mladen Naletilic commanded the Convicts Battalion? Quite the reverse. Which evidence was produced by the Prosecution to establish beyond any reasonable doubt the responsibility of Mladen Naletilic for the conflicts in Sovici and Doljani? Please, a name, just one name of one witness for the Prosecution who proved the comprehensive, the all round command role of Mladen Naletilic in Sovici and Doljani, one Prosecution witness who would prove unambiguously beyond any doubt that he commanded the Convicts Battalion. Perhaps witnesses who recounted the events in Doljani, but it happened on the 20th of April, when Mladen Naletilic was not there, because after the 19th, when he came to get the -- his friend's son who was with the Convicts Battalion, from day one, who was to take his friend's dead son to his father, and we established that after 19th of April, neither Mladen Naletilic nor the Convicts Battalion ever returned, and I believe we've already shown the whole road covered by the Convicts Battalion, what it was, where it was, and what it did. So please, what evidence was produced here that Mladen Naletilic had anything to do with civilians in Sovici? I showed you a videotape -- I showed you a videotape during Dr. Bagaric's testimony. It was a tape of the gentleman in the Prosecution, and after him, all the witnesses who were paraded through this courtroom, including the Prosecution's witness, Safet Idrizovic, the exchange was agreed at the highest military and political level. There was an exchange of the population between Sovici Muslims on the one hand, therefore, and the Croats from Konjic, Jablanica and so on and so forth, on the other hand. And what does Mladen Naletilic have to do with this? But the Prosecutor keeps claiming the opposite, I don't know, on the basis of what evidence. The BH Army -- but excuse me, after the conflict which happened and it's been described how I won't bother you with this, heads are falling, there are clashes, what was the HVO to do to satisfy the Prosecutor? To avoid any confusion. A person under arms, whether in a uniform or not, and the BH Army liked to change dress and they all frequently did it from civilian into uniforms and from uniforms to civilians to show they were civilians when they needed that. So naturally the military police would take them for investigation. Did anyone ill treat them during that time? Well excuse me, why don't these gentlemen prove it? Did anyone ill treat them during that procedure? Please, let somebody prove it, but what does my client have to do with it? Why, you heard here clear evidence, people who took them to the investigating prison in Ljubuski. What were they to do, to release them and say, sorry, just kidding, a mistake. But of course, there is something which is called military investigation because heads had fallen, heads were rolling. But if somebody ill treated them during that, when they were being taken in and in some further proceedings, well, let them be punished. I have nothing against it. Quite the contrary. We've heard that. But what evidence did we hear that my client had something to do with it? We didn't hear who took them away, when, how and so on. Look at the first statements they gave after coming out of those prisons, camps, or returns home when they gave their first statements to the AID. We did not produce them but we used them in our cross-examinations. Whoever mentioned my client? It was all at a later stage, having returned, they all put stories together. They watched television or read newspapers. And it was then that they learned without having ever seen him before, had they seen him before they would have said it right away. What comes as a surprise again is that the Prosecutor also claims that after the first operation in Doljani, Mladen Naletilic had ordered the second operation, and ordered that there should be no survivors and that that second attack followed a few days after the 20th of April. Who is it that did not survive? Which are the houses that were torched after that when we heard all that happened and everything that happened on the 17th, 18th and 19, which were the witnesses testifying here who could confirm that? Not a single one. The Defence, in contrast, showed that Mladen Naletilic neither commanded nor ordered the operations in Doljani on the 20th of April and what is abundantly clear is that this operation did not take place on the 20th of April but the one that I mentioned earlier, the 30th of July, 1993, and that is when the BH Army attacked Doljani and committed the massacre that I spoke about. That was the second operation in Doljani. Yes. But it was committed by the BH Army, and yet it's said it liberated Doljani. I don't know from whom did it liberate it from. It liberated it from all the civilians, presumably, whom they put in camps and some were liberated of their lives. Ergo, since there is no evidence for this, the Prosecutor continues, even at the end of the case, persists in his claims basing it on the testimony of just one witness, because even the witnesses for the Prosecution did not confirm it, and that one we don't we know it, it is Falk Simang, of course. The Prosecutor persists in claiming, after all that he heard, after all the documents that he saw, which were produced, which were admitted, which their witness Safet Idrizovic gave to the OTP and we got them at the end of the case, of course, because had we had them for our cross-examination, it would have been completely different of course, but what can we do? And it clearly says who sent buses, who ordered civilians to leave Sovici and so on and so forth. I don't want to wear you down with all this because it is all common knowledge. Then why does the Prosecutor persist even though he has seen documents signed by the command of the HVO as such, Mr. Petkovic, who confirms that it was an agreement between Petkovic and Halilovic at the highest political and military level. And this exchange did take place but how the Muslims came to Jablanica but the Croats, by Jove, never arrived at Konjic because there is nothing else. And then another attempt. Well, perhaps it will pass muster. No. War doesn't break out overnight. It always has its roots and its reasons, but these reasons are certainly not those that the Prosecutor says they are, and that is that it was the persecution policy which Mladen Naletilic ordered and carried out. What was that policy? Let me say I could give you a hundred examples, but also let me tell you that something else happened and that, again, is common knowledge. In January, after the Vance-Owen Plan which was to be implemented, the OTP calls it an ultimatum, and after that, forgets to say that we had a witness here who issued that order. We heard Bozo Rajic's testimony. He is the author of that order. And he is the only person who can talk about that. It was no the OTP who was there in Mostar, but it was Bozo Rajic who actually wrote that and who explained to the honourable Chamber what had happened. What I ask from the BH Army I asked from the HVO, and I acted in accordance with the agreement regarding those provinces, and in that division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the mediation of the international community starting with Cutilheiro to Vance-Owen, what was happening? In January of 1993, Muslims finally became aware that the unitarian Bosnia-Herzegovina would fall through, and that is the only thing that they ever wanted from the very first day until this very day, and still today. And they realised that the international community would divide Bosnia-Herzegovina, not Milosevic and Tudjman. They were just small fish for the international community which eventually proved to be truth. It was the international community who divided it because they realised that the three peoples had to agree how they would live together within the recognised external borders, and they realised that the only way to do it was to divide Bosnia-Herzegovina. Finally Muslims realised that the unitarian Bosnia-Herzegovina had ceased to exist and that it was over, and the -- at the time, they had ten time stronger armed forces than the HVO. They created the positions for themselves and they wanted to occupy the territories and they turned against the weakest body in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Who was that in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time? Who was the smallest? Who was the weakest? Croats, of course. They accounted for only 17 per cent at the time. Today they account for only 10 per cent. Where have the 7 per cent gone? You have heard our expert demographer, an United Nations expert, who has answered that question: Where have the 7 per cent of Croats gone in the meantime? Would it be logical for the smallest people to turn against the strongest people? Is there any sense to that? Of course, it was the army with the Neretva 1993 plan that started the offensive. We heard the testimony of Sefer Halilovic who was the main commander of the BH Army. When was that plan launched? In January 1993 they cleansed the entire area from Konjic and now they had to do it in Mostar. Why Mostar? Because they couldn't get to the sea if Mostar wasn't theirs. I won't belabour on that because I do not have the time to go into the details of the Neretva 1993 but this is a fact. There is no doubt about that, regardless of what the OTP may claim, regardless of what the judgement that would interfere with the future course of history could bring. We had just -- we heard testimonies by experts, historian who explained it all too well to us, how the Bosniak nation came to be. It is still in the process of being created. That process has not been completed yet. The Bosniak nation is still being born. And in that light, the way the OTP wanted and tried to represent things goes in favour of supporting that myth of the creation of the Bosniak army -- nation and that -- but there is a fact that the BH Army was the first to launch an attack, on this is a fact beyond any dispute. Why else would it -- then the meeting took place in Medjugorje on 17 May when Stoltenberg Tudjman and Alija Izetbegovic met. What did they do there on the 17th of May? They still implemented the Vance-Owen Plan. Nothing happened before that. And then the BH Army attacked on the 30th of June for reasons known only to them, purportedly to liberate Mostar. From whom? Bijelo Polje, Vrapcici, they again committed atrocious massacres, the HVO and the BH Army were together in the trenches, the BH Army imprisoned all the civilians in various camps. And that is when the war started, on the 30th of June, this was followed by the Owen Stoltenberg plan which is an union of three republics. That was the end of provinces. And then there was a free for all to grab as many territories as possible. If you look at the map and if you see how the HVO was withdrawing at the time, you would be clear on how things happened. On the one hand, on the left flank, from Kupres, the Army of Republika Srpska; and on the other hand, the BH Army. That was a battle for territory. The citizens of the same state, they were all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and when the citizens of one state wage war for anything, this time it was a war for territories, then obviously we end up with a civil war. It is what Martin Garrod said. And we have to be clear on that. Why would it take an international conflict to do that? Maybe to thank the Republic of Croatia for accepting over a million of their refugees, for spending over a billion dollars in order to provide for the Muslim refugees in Croatia, for having armed them, for having stopped the aggression launched by the army of the Republika Srpska, for having accepted them, saved them and armed them. And this purportedly was done by the country that had a de facto plan of conquering them, on the following day. And this all happened before the referendum, the underlying idea was for the Croats to vote in the referendum. What if the Croats didn't vote? Hadn't voted in the referendum? Bosnia and Herzegovina would have remained in Yugoslavia. It would have never been internationally recognised. And the break-up from Yugoslavia would have been called secession, and then both the HVO and the BH Army would have been called terrorists. However, when the referendum was over, and when the Croats voted 100 per cent in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina, mind you these same people are alleged to have had a plan of conquering that same state on the following day. Then the tables turned and the policy changed. And then the HZ HB was proclaimed, God knows what kind of a concoction, however, the HVO was as legal as the BH Army. The Army of Republika Srpska was not as legal as both the HVO and the BH Army. All the three were the armies of one and the same state, you know. I was surprised to hear yesterday that the Prosecutor claims that it doesn't really matter who attacked whom first. I've been in criminal law for 25 years. I've practised in other states, not only in mine. Let me just give you an example. If two people fight in a pub, and when one of them draws a weapon, does the other person have the right to self defence? And now the Prosecutor claims that it doesn't matter who was it the first who attacked. It does matter, if the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the first one who launched the attack, we heard witnesses who testified to the fact that the first attack was planned for the 19th of April, and then the 9th of May and so on and so forth. Then it is very logical that in such a state of chaos where the fighting was carried out in order to preserve every single house, when -- on the 9th of May, 70 Croats were killed by sniper fire. So there was street fighting in the heart of Mostar, on the western side of Mostar. And then we are surprised when civilians who wore civilian clothes, but still they were soldiers but they just wore civilian clothes. We heard Witness O who claimed he was a civilian but he was a military commander, and he was responsible for crimes because he was the one who pursued exactly that criminal policy of conquering territories and creating a better position for the future negotiations. So what should -- what was the HVO supposed to do? They were supposed to make arrests and to verify who was a soldier, who was not a soldier. This is what they did on the 9th of May, and if they established that somebody was a civilian they would release them. The only one -- the only ones arrested were the members of the BH Army who were then investigated and prosecuted by the military court. On the 30th of June, they reattacked and when the Muslims from the western bank were called, as we heard from one witness, when asked who was to blame for their lot, they said, Arif Pasalic, commander of the fourth corps. So again, arrests were made in order to verify who was a soldier, who wasn't, and they were then all released during July and August, all those who were not members of the BH Army, and 448 and you will now ask me how I know that figure, documents were found in Jablanica, so the 448 were released because they were members of the BH Army. The only document that says that they were 1500 is the document by the Red Cross but we had a witness here who was testifying in a closed session, who launched an initiative to release 700 or 800 people, and that is then when they 448 remained and they were members of the BH Army. The Prosecution ignores something that this honourable Chamber shouldn't ignore and that is that no conflict, no operation launched by the HVO was targeted against the civilian population. The Prosecution claims that everything was targeted against the civilians, that is the Muslim civilians. He ignores the fact that in any armed conflict, which is necessary for this discussion to take place in front of you, Your Honours, that there should be two sides to each conflict. And they indeed existed. One of them was the BH Army and the other was the HVO. It was not the Muslim civilians on the one hand and the Croat civilians on the other hand. The fact that the atrocities of that war affected civilians is only a misfortunate consequence of that war rather than a part of the planned policy of the Croatian side to that conflict. The Defence brought witnesses who have direct knowledge of the beginning of the conflict in May, on the 9th of May, how the BH Army launched the attack because that is very important for the decision of this Trial Chamber, and the picture that they will get about that conflict. We had a witness here, NP, who clearly said before all of you what his role was with regard to Vranica and the role of the notorious Juka Prazina, and even that even after that, the Prosecution persists in their allegations. Based on all the evidence regarding Mostar, can the Trial Chamber now make a decision that will proclaim Mladen Naletilic responsible for the events that took place on the 9th of May? Can you, Your Honours, find him responsible for Heliodrom? If nothing else, we explored the issue of Heliodrom to the tiniest detail. Was it Mladen Naletilic who set up Heliodrom? Was it Mladen Naletilic who controlled it? Was it Mladen Naletilic who sent people there? Mladen Naletilic never saw Heliodrom, was never there, and I believe that we have been able to establish at least that through all of our witnesses and through all the evidence presented to you. So the Defence respectfully submits that such a decision cannot be made, and the burden of proof lies with the Prosecution and the Prosecution has failed to produce evidence that would justify a conviction on this count. And now let's move on to documents, to some of the exhibits very briefly. The exhibits are not consistent, mutually consistent, and they are not consistent with the testimonies of the witnesses. The Prosecutor's witnesses were not able to confirm the authenticity of the documents because they didn't write it, and they didn't know anything about the circumstances under which these documents were compiled. The authenticity of any document can be confirmed only by the author of such a document, who can also confirm the veracity of such a document, and that is that that document has been signed by that person personally and stamped by the institution which OTP witness could confirm the authenticity of any of the documents? They bombarded us with piles and piles of documents, of exhibits, and we have established what we have established. As far as the reliability of documents provided by SpaBat and other international forces, Mr. Meek has referred to those, and we also refer to those in our closing argument, and as for the source, as for the -- in our closing brief, and Van der Grinten's source were usually his interpreters and he didn't verify any of the contents. He just took the contents for granted. And that is more or less how the international observers compiled their documents. We heard a lot about SpaBat. We heard Van der Grinten who -- we heard Garrod who was not in Mostar at the time, referred to by the indictment. He was in Mostar very short -- for a short period of time, then he went to Zenica and returned to Mostar only in 1994. He doesn't know anything about what happened in Mostar in 1993. The Prosecutor also quotes presidential transcripts. The position of the Defence about the presidential transcripts is the same. The OTP could only refer to those presidential transcripts which speak of the territory mentioned in the indictment and the period of time mentioned in the indictment; however, they didn't do that. The persons mentioned in the transcripts talked about the reliability of these transcripts. When we talk about the transcripts, we have to mention Mr. Pasalic, who said that he didn't -- not that he didn't like what he read but he knows better than the Prosecutor what the truth is, and what he was bothered with when he testified, that is Mr. Pasalic, was the lies in the transcript and the fact that some things were taken out of the context. And Mr. Pasalic, and all the other people mentioned in the transcript, can say whether these transcripts are authentic or not. It is not to -- up to the Prosecutor to say that. The Prosecutor should have called the people who were present at those meetings and they then could have said whether these transcripts were authentic or not. If the Honourable Chamber wants to rely any of their decisions on any of these presidential transcripts, then they have to first verify whether these transcripts are integral, whether they have been translated properly, whether the translations are true to the Croatian originals, and furthermore, the Trial Chamber will have to make sure that every transcript has a beginning and a -- the end. Let me illustrate -- point to the transcript PT 8 from an alleged meeting between Alija Izetbegovic, Siljeg Boban, Susak and President Tudjman, which purportedly took place in Tudjman's residence. That meeting took place on the 28th of March, 1993. It hasn't been translated. So if the OTP wants to talk about the ultimatum which allegedly the HVO imposed on the BH Army, then the Prosecutor should have translated this transcript to the full. As things stand now, only those parts have been translated that support the OTP's thesis but not the integral document. The presidential transcript PT 8.1 is the transcript which was given to the Defence for the first time for the cross-examination of expert Ancic in September 2002. He was the last witness and we were left without the possibility to refute any of the allegations found in that alleged transcript. However, let us say that that transcript has also not been translated. The first 16 pages have not been translated at all. I apologise. It is PT28. I'm talking about the presidential transcript PT28. And then, a part was taken from page 14 and in the English version, it is the beginning of the entire document marked as PT28. Somebody unknown to the Defence has compiled this transcript by shifting the text from the -- from page 13 to page 1, and nobody knows - allegedly these are the words of a president - nobody knows which president it is. Pages from 0157968 to 0157979 have not been translated at all. And again, nothing from 0157983 to 0157986, has been translated. The entire end of the transcript is missing. In the English version, from page -- the last three digits 991 to the page 801. I have some other documents which I would like to show you as an example of something that the Prosecutor referred to yesterday. I won't have the time to show them all to you. Can we please turn the ELMO on? I would like to show you some typical examples. Can we please have the ELMO turned on? In the technical booth, can we please have the ELMO switched on? Why am I telling you all this? Because I believe, Your Honours, that every document has to be double-checked by you, together with a court interpreter, because you have to look not only at the English version but also at the Croatian version because you have to make sure that everything has been translated. Why am I telling you that? This is a typical example. Look at the first page of this document. Then look at the second page of the same document. This page ends in a number 52 and then half of the page is missing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the counsel unfortunately, because he's too far away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, you have to speak directly into the microphone, otherwise we could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, look, the entire page is empty. Then there is an item 6 here and it says, "Documents to be sent to" -- can you please follow the English version, in the English version you can't see this empty page. It says here, "To the sent to the ZP Mostar, the ATG Tuta and OS." And the translators, translated that as the intelligence service. Why? I believe and I claim that this is the operative headquarters. Why has this been translated in this way? No signature, no stamp. And the date is the 29th December of 1993. And the ATG Tuta which never existed for that matter, and on the 23rd of December, the Convicts Battalion also didn't exist because that was after the reorganisation had been carried out. So let's move on to show you another typical document. Look at this. There are a number of such documents. The contents in this case is not important even though it's quite nice. This is Mr. Andabak, who is requesting the punishment of a man who wanted to make a gift of a stolen car to the Convicts Battalion. So quite curious. But here we see Mr. Even Andabak's signature. You don't have to know Croatian to see that. But what is typed is Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Now look at the translation. Look at the translation. Where does it say that we have the handwritten signature of Ivan Andabak's? Now, I can show you the next document. Again, Ivan Andabak, the next document, Ivan Andabak. And so on, to your heart's content. Everywhere we have typed "Naletilic" of course, but no where in translation, only "Naletilic." So please check the document the, the two -- take into consideration, please go through them with translators. That is why I said I did not really trust the bona fides of the Prosecutor. And these are only minor characteristic examples. Your Honours, I have to conclude my closing argument. I have another 15 minutes only. And it seems that as usual, I didn't prepare properly because there are very many things which I have not had time to say but I do not think that it is all that important because I'm sure Your Honours that you will do that in your thorough analysis of these documents. So let me start taking -- bringing things to the end and to say the HZ HB has absolutely justified its existence. In every document, it points out that it is a provisional organisation, so thank God that it existed because it saved many lives, because it has fed many people, it was the only door to then Bosnia-Herzegovina such as it was at the time. It never asked for international recognition. It never occurred to do so but the international community, the moment that Mr. Mate Boban was officially invited to official negotiations recognised his status just as it recognised the status of Alija Izetbegovic as a representative of one people only, which he exclusively called the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and therefore he named his army exclusively the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the same holds true of the gentleman from Republika Srpska. In the Washington Agreement, they recognised all the laws as de facto and de jure in Herceg-Bosna, they recognised that the right to the confederation -- of the federation of the Muslims and Croats with the Republic of Croatia. That was the international community which recognised that. It recognises all its laws as confirmed by the Dayton Accords and these laws are still in force, some of them, not all of them. What the Prosecutor is trying to say has nothing to do with the reality or the truth. And let me gradually draw this to a close and say that I am aware of the time allotted for the closing arguments. Of course, I am not able to reproduce hundreds and thousands of transcripts or documents and I could not do it in my closing brief, again because of the limited number of pages, but I am confident that this Honourable Chamber will not base its decision on some documents, on a sentence pronounced by a witness here and there, but on the whole material of the case by properly weighing the -- weighing the evidence produced and that it will base its decisions in -- on the principle that governs all the criminal cases, and which can be summed up as in dubio pro reo, which means when in doubt, we decide in favour of the accused. Mladen Naletilic did not set out to prove that he was not guilty. He did not assume the role of a Prosecutor and the burden of proof. Mladen Naletilic offered a picture of the events which unfolded during the time covered by the indictment, such as it was, and in that picture, his role as the commander of the Convicts Battalion, and as the chief figure carrying out Franjo Tudjman's policy in the persecution of Muslims and the creation of greater Croatia is no where to be found there, just as Greater Croatia is no where to be found, because there were never such an intent as history shows. The Republic of Croatia was the first one to recognise Bosnia-Herzegovina and all the rest, I won't repeat all that it did. And the banovina, I know it is very difficult to understand the history of those lands but when one doesn't understand it then why doesn't he ask those who do understand it and they will explain what is banovina, how did it come into being, and under what circumstances? That banovina does not at all look like the HZ HB. My client, Mladen Naletilic, cannot be found at any meeting, anywhere. So what is this figure my client? He's not at a meeting of the smallest possible unit let alone staff or brigade or Ministry of Defence. So whence his power? Is it some magic wand? I presume it must be some magic wand. Because I don't know, let me try to illustrate. How could Mladen Naletilic -- let's take, let's take for instance he's the Convicts Battalion's commander in 1993. Let's take that. Now, how is it that Mladen Naletilic decided suddenly to attack Sovici? Now that we know that there is an operative zone 1, second operative zone, main staff, Ministry of Defence. And now he comes and what does it mean that he can go wherever he pleases and attack whomever he pleases? Like Ali Baba and his 40 men? We have shown how the HVO structure functioned, and in that structure, in 1993, my client is not to be found, and even if he were to be found, nobody could say, and there were witnesses who spoke about this for days on end, how the orders went through a chain of command, who held the front lines, what happened to units which came to the front line, who they were subordinated to and so on and so forth. Mladen Naletilic is not to be found in any HDZ meeting. It is claimed here the HDZ knows who but we heard testimony that he was never even a member of the HDZ let alone attended its meeting. And listen, what is the most important thing of all, when one looks at the documents. Let's try and find a single one that my client, Mladen Naletilic, is the addressee of a document to which the Prosecutor refers? And finally, Your Honours, the last thing I wish to say in conclusion, in view of all the above said, the Defence suggests to the Court the only possible sentence, and that is acquittal. I do not doubt at all -- I do not doubt at all -- that if you find some evidence, although the evidence -- the Defence doesn't see them but perhaps you will look at them with a different eyes but we believe that you will -- that in the name of justice, in the name of truth, you will acquit my client, and I never doubted that. And this acquittal -- yesterday I must say that I felt rather moved, perhaps it was the only thing which was beyond the professional attitude, that Mladen Naletilic is not going back as a victor. Victor of? Are we talking here about a battle? About a sports match? Who is a winner and who is a loser in this game? He will return to Mostar acquitted and the victory will be the victory of the Statute and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. That is the only possible victor. Yesterday, theatrically a photograph was presented and I don't know why. It was held like this but has the Prosecutor ever said which year was it made? He owns -- produces the effect to show it to everybody, do you know which, when was it done? The OTP does know it but true to their style, they don't say it. It is 1992, after the liberation of Mostar. Everybody who had some merit had it, I don't know if that is the custom in other countries but in coffee shops they put up posters of people of merit, and it says, "Our victory," yes, the victory of the day of the liberation of Mostar. Then -- but they end up in their style victor, over whom? What does this poster have to do, has the OTP ever established when it was done, even though we know that it was 1992 but since 1992 to this day somebody perhaps still has it at his coffee shop. And why not? I'd like to conclude by addressing you, Your Honours with a comment that you made which gave me strength, I must say, and you always instill me with strength, whenever I stumbled, whenever I was at the end of my forces, you encouraged me, your comments, your suggestions, always helped me to persist. When the witness Ancic testified quite recently you will remember when it was said that it all depended on the lawyers skill, you then bravely valiantly and one could see that you were speaking from the heart, that it came from a man who loved the truth, that the Chamber cannot be manipulated. That the performance is not the key, that skill is not the key, that the only key is the evidence, and this set my mind at peace. I felt calmer when I started my closing argument, especially having heard the closing argument of my learned friends from the OTP. The Defence believes this comment and believes that a good moving -- and moving performance does not mean the accolade -- the applause at the end of that performance. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tomorrow, we will hear the closing arguments from the Defence counsel of Mr. Martinovic. So we'll resume tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 in the same courtroom.
